findings.explanation: Splunkbase app 1747 is the Splunk Add-on for Cisco WSA (Splunk_TA_cisco-wsa); REST API Modular Input is Splunkbase app 1546 (rest_ta). The same wrong ID is repeated in detailedImplementation Prerequisites and in the first references entry title and URL.
findings.quote: Use the Splunk **REST API Modular Input** ([Splunkbase app ID 1747](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1747))
findings.suggested_fix: Replace every 1747 link and label with REST API Modular Input, https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1546, in dataSources, detailedImplementation and references.

findings.explanation: The Authentication data model describes login attempts (action, user, src, dest of an authentication event). A polled visitor-badge record with an expiry date and status is an inventory/state record, not an authentication attempt, so the mapping and the dataModelAcceleration advice to accelerate Authentication for `vms:visitor` rows would mislead implementers.
findings.suggested_fix: Set cimModels to an empty list (no CIM model fits a visitor-credential inventory) and rewrite dataModelAcceleration to say the search runs on raw `index=physical` events; only badge-reader access attempts (not this feed) would be candidates for Authentication.

findings.explanation: `indexes_search` is not a Splunk capability; index access is granted with `srchIndexesAllowed` in authorize.conf (or the role's Indexes tab). `dispatch_rest_to_indexers` is unrelated to running this search, and mapping an analyst role to `sc_admin` grants full Splunk Cloud admin rights.
findings.quote: RBAC: grant `indexes_search` on `physical` and `dispatch_rest_to_indexers` only to the `physical_security_analyst` role (map to `sc_admin` patterns on Splunk Cloud).
findings.suggested_fix: Say: create or reuse a role with `srchIndexesAllowed = physical` (Settings > Roles > Indexes) and no admin capabilities; on Splunk Cloud inherit from `user`, not `sc_admin`.

findings.explanation: description (and knownFalsePositives, which keys on `host`, `count` and `span=1h`) describe an aggregation that is not in the SPL; the SPL is a per-row filter on `status="active"` and `days_to_exp < 1` with a `table` of `visitor_id`, `host_employee`, `badge_expiry`, `days_to_exp`.
findings.quote: grouped by `entity`. Outputs `count` each `the scheduled window`
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual output: one row per active visitor badge whose `badge_expiry` date is today or in the past, listing visitor, sponsoring employee and days past expiry. Rewrite false positives around the same fields.

findings.explanation: None of the four scenarios names a real cause of a false expired-but-active row; they are generic metric-alert templates. Real causes for this search include visitor management API sync lag after checkout, the `badge_expiry` date being in UTC versus local time (round() moves badges expiring later today into the result), multi-day visitors whose expiry was extended in the PACS but not the visitor system, and older polled snapshots still showing `status=active`.
findings.quote: Batch `count` on `vms:visitor`** — Scheduled automation elevates `days_to_exp` without crossing `days_to_exp` < 0
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with those concrete causes and a suppression keyed on `visitor_id` (for example a short-lived lookup of extended visits) rather than a `host`-keyed exception register.

findings.explanation: props.conf sourcetype overrides do not change the string format of an extracted field, so this step cannot make `strptime` work. If the API returns ISO-8601 timestamps (with time and zone), `strptime(badge_expiry,"%Y-%m-%d")` will not parse and the rows silently drop out of the `where` clause.
findings.quote: Forwarders should tag `meta` sourcetype overrides in `props.conf` so search-time `strptime(badge_expiry,"%Y-%m-%d")` aligns with the API’s date format.
findings.suggested_fix: Tell the reader to confirm the exact `badge_expiry` format in a sample event and, if it is not `YYYY-MM-DD`, normalise it at ingest (for example with an INGEST_EVAL or a calculated field) or note that the SPL format string must match.

findings.explanation: The time range bounds when poll events were indexed, not when badges expired. With a one- to five-minute poll, 24 hours of events contains hundreds of snapshots per visitor, so the table repeats each visitor and still lists visitors whose older snapshots said `active` even after they were deactivated.
findings.quote: save as an alert with `dispatch.earliest_time=-24h` and `dispatch.latest_time=now` to catch badges that expired within the last day while still marked active.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain that the alert should evaluate only the latest snapshot per `visitor_id` (window equal to the poll interval, or latest-per-visitor logic) and that the 24h window is not an expiry window. Flag the SPL change to the human owner.

findings.explanation: The app field names the data source, not the Splunk component the reader installs.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the collection component, for example "REST API Modular Input (Splunkbase 1546) or HTTP Event Collector, polling the visitor management system API".

findings.explanation: Splunk Enterprise has no native REST polling input, and this documentation page name does not match a known Getting Data In topic; the link may 404 or redirect.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the URL; if it does not resolve to a real page, replace it with the REST API Modular Input Splunkbase page or the HTTP Event Collector documentation.

findings.explanation: Notables are a Splunk Enterprise Security concept; the UC lists no premium app and is otherwise a plain scheduled alert.
findings.quote: attach a runbook link in the notable description
findings.suggested_fix: Say "in the alert description" or state that ES is optional.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `days_to_exp < 0 OR days_to_exp < 1` is redundant (equivalent to `days_to_exp < 1`), and the search has no `dedup visitor_id` / `stats latest(*) by visitor_id`, so repeated polls duplicate rows and stale `status=active` snapshots produce false positives.
The Authentication tstats by user/action/src has no relationship to visitor badge expiry and returns nothing derived from `vms:visitor`; it should be removed with the Authentication mapping.

summary: The SPL idea (active visitor badges past their expiry date) is sound, but the add-on ID points to the Cisco WSA add-on, the CIM mapping to Authentication does not fit a badge-status inventory, the RBAC guidance names a capability that does not exist, and description and false-positive text describe fields (`entity`, `count`, `host`) the search never uses.
